A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BID research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison despite the revised title and appendix organization.

before.justification: v3 reports original diagnostic simulations, robot manipulation benchmarks, ablations and two real-world robot experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original simulation, benchmark, ablation and real-world experimental results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations 5–7 retain the same candidate sampling, backward coherence, strong/weak-policy forward contrast and action selection procedure. The revised dynamics models concern the theoretical analysis, not a changed BID algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same diagnostic simulation, Push-T, five RoboMimic tasks, Franka Kitchen and two real-world tasks, including the existing noise and moving-target scenarios. The added distribution-shift discussion introduces no new evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: The Diffusion Policy comparison retains Vanilla, Warmstart and EMA. The VQ-BeT experiments and both real-world tasks also retain their respective comparator sets.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation settings remain unchanged, including 100-episode simulation evaluations, 20-episode real-world comparisons, model configurations, noise levels and sample-size sweeps. Experimental details move from Appendix B to Appendix C.

E4.justification: Figure 7 and Appendix A retain the same scalability, compatibility, horizon/context, forward-contrast, EMA-decay, noise and distance-metric analyses. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Three-seed averaging, existing error bars and tabulated uncertainty reporting are retained. Neither run-count disclosures nor statistical estimation procedures change.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and experimental plots retain their results. For example, Table 1 reports closed-loop BID success rates of 54.4%, 45.3% and 31.7% at the same three noise levels in both versions; the reported 32% and 46% relative gains also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 assumes accurate implicit dynamics and expresses Proposition 1 using Pf^(2d) and Pb^(2d). v4 distinguishes training, test and learned dynamics, introduces forward/backward model-error terms, and replaces these powers with time-indexed products involving P(P + delta). Section 3.2 and Appendix E substantially revise assumptions, observation-advantage conditioning, equality conditions in Propositions 6–7, Corollaries 2–3 and 10, and their proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the reactivity problem from stochastic environments to unexpected states arising from modeling errors or environmental stochasticity. The two main contributions, BID mechanism and empirical performance claims remain intact.

C2.justification: v3 primarily contrasts deterministic consistency benefits with stochastic reactivity costs. v4's Remarks 2–3 explain that modeling errors or distribution shift can disadvantage long horizons even in deterministic environments, while their benefits require accurate inference and diversity of past strategies. This substantially revises the analysis's applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware descriptions, checkpoint information, data-collection details and code-access disclosures are retained. Table 6 keeps the same hyperparameters; relocating the implementation appendix does not add reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work comparisons are unchanged. The discussion positioning BID against receding horizon and temporal ensembling moves from Section 4.3 to Appendix B without substantive revision.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Closed-Loop Resampling' to 'Guided Test-Time Sampling.' Section 4.3 moves to a new appendix, assumptions are consolidated in Appendix E.1, and subsequent appendices are renumbered. Local prose, conference-header and correspondence edits accompany the theoretical revisions.

P2.justification: All 15 figures and six tables retain their scientific content and display structure. Conference formatting, spacing and text reflow alter their presentation and placement relative to surrounding paragraphs, without adding or redrawing scientific displays.

improvement.justification: v4 usefully extends v3's exact-dynamics analysis to modeling errors and distribution shift and qualifies when longer horizons help. However, the revised mismatch-term simplifications in Appendix E.3, pages 30 and 32, use a product/complement identity that is not generally valid for multi-step horizons. This leaves the proof support for the central extension unresolved. With the algorithm and empirical evidence unchanged, the theoretical gains and introduced proof defects do not yield a reliably assessable net quality change.
